root_cause.summary: Port collision, not a dependency regression. :5173 was held by an unrelated stale dev server (another project's Vite, pid 317796 alive since 2026-09-17) → this app's Vite fell back to :5174 → two hardcoded 5173 assumptions broke.
root_cause.a: backend/src/index.ts dev allowlist was the closed list ['http://localhost:3000','http://localhost:5173','http://localhost'] → no Access-Control-Allow-Origin for origin http://localhost:5174.
root_cause.b: vite.config.ts pinned server.hmr.clientPort: 5173 → the HMR socket targeted the OTHER project's server ('WebSocket closed without opened').
root_cause.evidence: ss -ltnp: [::1]:5174 pid=324645 (this app) vs *:5173 pid=317796 (currencyExchange Vite); the pre-existing backend on :3001 reproduced the missing ACAO.

R1.requirement: Development CORS must accept any loopback port (localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1, any port) and still refuse remote or look-alike origins.
R1.test: backend/src/__tests__/corsOrigins.test.ts › 'R1 · development accepts any local port' (3 tests, asserted through the REAL cors middleware)
R1.change: backend/src/utils/corsOrigins.ts — dev branch returns anchored patterns instead of an exact-port list

R2.requirement: Production allowlist must stay an exact-match list: CORS_ORIGIN (trailing slash normalized) + comma-separated CORS_ORIGINS (invalid entries dropped) + explicit ALLOW_LOCALHOST opt-in, and must still throw when nothing is configured. No RegExp may leak into production.
R2.test: backend/src/__tests__/corsOrigins.test.ts › 'R2 · production allowlist stays exact and explicit' (5 tests)
R2.change: verbatim extraction of normalizeOrigin + production branch, no semantic change

R3.requirement: The Vite dev server must fail fast instead of silently drifting to another port, and HMR must never pin a clientPort the HTTP server may not own.
R3.change: vite.config.ts — added server.strictPort: true, removed server.hmr.clientPort

red_green.red: pnpm vitest run backend/src/__tests__/corsOrigins.test.ts src/__tests__/devServerConfig.test.ts → exit 1, 4 failed / 7 passed: 'http://localhost:5174: expected undefined to be http://localhost:5174', same for 127.0.0.1:5174, plus strictPort + clientPort guards. The extraction was first written with the OLD dev list so RED exposed the logic gap, not a missing module. The 'refuses remote origins' guard already passed in RED (no false positives).
